Only my `FastDateFormatAgentTest.java` exists as an `*AgentTest.java` file, so this confirms the full suite run matches the isolated run: 35 passing, 3 failing on genuine bugs.

I wrote `src/test/org/apache/commons/lang/time/FastDateFormatAgentTest.java` (JUnit 3.8 style, matching the project's existing tests), covering caching/identity, `equals`/`hashCode`, accessors, pattern parsing, numeric/text field formatting cross-checked against `SimpleDateFormat`, time zone name/offset rules, literal quoting, `format(Object/Date/Calendar/long)` dispatch and error cases, and `parseObject`. 35 of 38 tests pass; 3 fail, each showing a real bug in `FastDateFormat`:

1. **`testGetMaxLengthEstimate_bug_ignoresPaddedFieldWidth`** — `PaddedNumberField.estimateLength()` always returns a constant `4` regardless of the field's actual padding width. For pattern `"yyyyy"` the formatted year is 5 characters (e.g. `"02023"`), exceeding `getMaxLengthEstimate()`, which violates the documented contract that the actual formatted length will almost always be `<=` the estimate.

2. **`testGetMaxLengthEstimate_bug_timeZoneColonVariantUnderestimated`** — `TimeZoneNumberRule.estimateLength()` returns a fixed `5` for both the `Z` and `ZZ` (colon) variants, but the colon variant (`"+05:30"`) is actually 6 characters, again violating the `getMaxLengthEstimate()` contract.

3. **`testUnterminatedQuote_bug_shouldRejectMalformedPattern`** — The class javadoc says patterns are compatible with `SimpleDateFormat` (aside from time zones). `SimpleDateFormat` rejects an unterminated quote (e.g. `"'abc"`) with `IllegalArgumentException`, but `FastDateFormat.parseToken()` silently swallows the rest of the pattern as a literal instead of flagging the malformed pattern.
